ks-gov-2026-holscher-cindy.name: Cindy Holscher
ks-gov-2026-holscher-cindy.bio: Kansas state senator elected in 2020; former Kansas House member who co-founded the Women's Bipartisan Caucus.

positions.stance: Lists cutting property taxes as a top commitment: "Rising taxes shouldn't push people out of their homes."
Pledges to make health care accessible and affordable: "Every Kansan should be able to take their child to the doctor."
"Kansas needs to stop approving new data centers until guardrails are in place."
Pledges to stand up to corruption: "It's time to end the sweetheart deals for billionaire CEOs."
Says the cost-of-living crisis is crushing Kansans and pledges to bring it under control.

ks-gov-2026-masterson-ty.name: Ty Masterson
ks-gov-2026-masterson-ty.bio: President of the Kansas Senate and former local official in Andover.

positions.stance: Proposes a Homeowners Bill of Rights "protecting homeowners from runaway property taxes" and giving taxpayers a stronger voice.
Proposes a Kansas Ratepayer Protection Pledge to protect families, farms, schools and businesses "from being stuck with higher costs created by powerful outside interests."

nm-gov-2026-hull-greggory.name: Greggory D. Hull
nm-gov-2026-hull-greggory.bio: Mayor of Rio Rancho, New Mexico.

positions.stance: Proposes "Four Steps to Zero" to phase out state tax on eligible personal income over four years while keeping net business profits taxable.
Will protect rural health systems, reform medical malpractice laws, lower prescription drug costs, and launch programs to recruit and retain doctors and nurses.
Will increase police presence statewide, enhance border security to end the fentanyl crisis, and set zero tolerance for violent crimes and crimes against children.
Will use targeted incentives to attract high-paying jobs and expand the state's energy portfolio to all sources "while unleashing our oil and gas operations."
Will invest in public education and demand accountability, expand tutoring, special education and Career Technical Education, and reform the Public Education Department.

nm-gov-2026-haaland-deb.name: Deb Haaland
nm-gov-2026-haaland-deb.bio: Former U.S. Secretary of the Interior and former U.S. Representative from New Mexico.

positions.stance: Plans to teach kids to read earlier, expand career pathways and community schools, and expand the Opportunity Scholarship to provide free tuition.
Would raise the minimum wage and child tax credit, ban AI rent-fixing algorithms, crack down on price gouging, and build more housing.
"As Governor, I will focus every day on stopping violent crime, getting guns and drugs off our streets, and addressing the root causes of crime."
Will fight to protect health care access and address the doctor shortage through interstate medical compacts, rural residencies, and loan repayment incentives.

ne-gov-2026-pillen-jim.name: Jim Pillen
ne-gov-2026-pillen-jim.bio: Governor of Nebraska since 2023; veterinarian and founder of Pillen Family Farms; former member of the Nebraska Board of Regents.

positions.stance: Would eliminate tax incentives for Big Tech data centers, lower property insurance rates, pursue "transformative property tax reform," and cut government spending.
"Making Nebraska Healthy Again": eliminate toxins in our food and in our water.
Would continue to strengthen community colleges and expand availability of workforce housing.
Would "keep boys out of girls' sports," protect life and the 2nd Amendment, and reform the ballot petition process.
Would ensure every 3rd grader reads on grade level and reform K-12 funding to mirror the community college model.

ne-gov-2026-walz-lynne.name: Lynne Walz
ne-gov-2026-walz-lynne.bio: Former teacher and Nebraska state legislator.

positions.stance: Says she is a leader "with a track record of putting parties aside to get results" and wants low taxes, strong schools, and a bustling economy.
Says leaders should respect voter-approved measures like medical marijuana, paid sick leave, minimum wage, and school vouchers: "When the voters speak, our job as representatives is to listen."
"I will fight for an honest, transparent government."
Will support and attract businesses and grow rural communities by investing in broadband, agriculture, and Main Street small businesses.
Says housing, childcare, health care and groceries are too expensive and will work with state and national leaders to address affordability.

id-gov-2026-little-brad.name: Brad Little
id-gov-2026-little-brad.bio: Governor of Idaho since 2019; lifelong rancher and businessman.

positions.stance: Says he cut or simplified 95 percent of Idaho regulations and is "going to keep on cutting red tape in the years ahead."
Cites teacher pay increases, literacy funding, and expanded school choice options for families, plus the Idaho LAUNCH program.
Cites historic tax relief and a balanced budget, "with plans to give more money back to the people through continued tax relief."
Says his LAUNCH program is a national model for putting President Trump's workforce strategy into action.
Says he is working with law enforcement and President Trump to fight the influence of Mexican drug cartels in Idaho.

id-gov-2026-pickens-terri.name: Terri Pickens
id-gov-2026-pickens-terri.bio: Founder of Pickens Law, P.A., a Boise litigation firm; former Nez Perce County public defender.

positions.stance: Supports small businesses, a stable tax structure, and "a system that works for everyday Idahoans, not billionaires," including fair treatment and a living wage.
Says Idaho workers "deserve fair wages, safe workplaces, and economic security" and supports strong unions and worker protections.
Supports repealing "the school voucher scheme," better education funding, higher teacher salaries, and funding for Pre-K and full-time kindergarten.
"Public lands must stay in the hands of the public, not privatized"; will fight to maintain access for recreation, hunting, and fishing.
Pledges to protect civil rights including freedom of speech, privacy, "freedom of choice and bodily autonomy," and freedom to marry.

id-ltgov-2026-bedke-scott.name: Scott Bedke
id-ltgov-2026-bedke-scott.bio: Lieutenant Governor of Idaho, elected in 2022; former Speaker of the Idaho House and cattle rancher.

positions.stance: Cites cutting regulations by 95%, a balanced budget, and Idaho's largest tax cut as House Speaker, and says he continues fighting for lower taxes.
Says he continues "fighting to stop liberal efforts to defund the police, to secure America's borders, and to keep Idaho families safe."
Cites an NRA A+ rating and 100% pro-life voting record, and says he fought Critical Race Theory in Idaho schools.
Calls water "the lifeblood of our state" and cites negotiating settlements on Idaho's longstanding water issues.
"Every Idaho student deserves a quality education"; cites increasing public school funding by over 60 percent as Speaker.
Would eliminate the General Excise Tax on food and medicine and freeze property taxes for kūpuna at retirement on their primary residence.
Would establish a Government Transparency Office, require annual audits of public-private partnerships, and forward corruption cases to the Attorney General.
Would deliver 15,000 fee-simple homes priced $400K–$600K through a Housing Master Plan, with permitting streamlining and an end to no-bid contracts.
Would renegotiate Hawaiian Homes Act terms, including blood quantum and land rights, and integrate Hawaiian language and culture into all schools.
Proposes financial literacy in every classroom, merit pay for teachers, proficiency-based graduation, and local budget autonomy for each island.

hi-gov-2026-green-josh.name: Josh Green
hi-gov-2026-green-josh.bio: Governor of Hawaii since 2022; former lieutenant governor, state legislator, and ER physician.

positions.stance: Cites delivering "the biggest tax cut for the middle class in Hawaii state history" and doubling the earned income and food tax credits.
Says he is bringing down housing costs by building at scale, including 46,000 affordable units, and cutting red tape on new housing.
Cites the largest state investment in reducing homelessness, including 30 kauhale tiny-home villages statewide.
Says he provides "steady leadership in a crisis," citing COVID, the Maui wildfires, and Oahu floods.
Says he is lowering health care costs by covering Obamacare subsidies and bringing nearly $1 billion in federal rural health investment.

nh-gov-2026-warmington-cinde.name: Cinde Warmington
nh-gov-2026-warmington-cinde.bio: Served as the only Democrat on the New Hampshire Executive Council.

positions.stance: "Your community. Your grid. Your rules."
"Standing up to Trump's chaos, costs, and corruption."
Proposes a Granite State Integrity Commitment to "stop the corruption and self-dealing."
"End the property tax-hiking voucher scheme."
"A roof over every head."

nh-gov-2026-ayotte-kelly.name: Kelly Ayotte
nh-gov-2026-ayotte-kelly.bio: Governor of New Hampshire; former New Hampshire Attorney General.

positions.stance: Says she fixed the broken bail system, strengthened efforts against drug trafficking, and is backing first responders.
"Kelly is holding the line against new taxes — no income tax, no sales tax, EVER!"
Cites historic education funding, removing cell phones from classrooms, expanded childcare scholarships, and efforts to improve kids' reading.
Says she is pushing utilities and regulators to lower costs and working to bring more energy to the state.
Cites funding mental health and substance use treatment, protecting Medicaid, and a federal award for a new health care program.
Will dismantle cartel networks, strengthen law enforcement, and increase support for addiction recovery and mental health services.
"He pledges to abolish the state income tax, slash unnecessary regulation, and cut the red tape that stifles economic growth."
Would refocus schools on reading, math and science, eliminate "woke" indoctrination, and support educational freedom and curriculum transparency.

me-gov-2026-pingree-hannah.name: Hannah M. Pingree
me-gov-2026-pingree-hannah.bio: Former Speaker of the Maine House and former director of the Governor's Office of Policy Innovation and the Future; has run a small business.

positions.stance: Would invest $100 million per year in housing development and hold utilities accountable by tying their profits to lower bills and better performance.
Says Maine should lead in "a human-centered approach to education in the age of AI," limiting classroom distractions and giving teachers a seat at the table.
Will guarantee every young Mainer access to a meaningful hands-on work experience, such as an internship or apprenticeship, by age 20.
Will create a public health insurance option, "a State-backed plan that puts patients before profits."
Would accelerate permit approvals, cut red tape, grow the homebuilding workforce, and reduce evictions and homelessness.

ri-gov-2026-guckian-aaron.name: Aaron C. Guckian
ri-gov-2026-guckian-aaron.bio: Educator and public servant with experience in government, banking, nonprofits, and statewide advocacy.

positions.stance: Would lower the cost of living by expanding housing options, reducing construction barriers, lowering utility expenses, and reining in health care costs.
Would prioritize investments in public schools, teacher support, and career-ready pathways including vocational and technical programs.
Would address shortages of primary care doctors and dentists: "It shouldn't take months to see a doctor or dentist."
Proposes targeted tax relief, reducing hidden fees, and cutting wasteful government spending.
Pledges to restore transparency and eliminate mismanagement: "Government must work for the people—not the other way around."
Plan for "Making Quality, Affordable Healthcare Accessible for All Rhode Islanders."
Plan for "Creating & Growing Good-Paying Jobs."
Plan for "Childcare and Transportation for Working Families."
Proposes a "$100 Million Proposal for Career and Technical Education."
Plan for "Affordable Utility Bills and a Clean Energy Future."

ri-ltgov-2026-loughlin-john.name: John J. Loughlin, II
ri-ltgov-2026-loughlin-john.bio: Retired U.S. Army Reserve lieutenant colonel, former NASA public affairs officer, former Rhode Island state representative, and former WPRO radio host.

positions.stance: Says of electric bills: "With my plan, we could cut your bill in half."

ri-ltgov-2026-matos-sabina.name: Sabina Matos
ri-ltgov-2026-matos-sabina.bio: Lieutenant Governor of Rhode Island since 2021; former Providence City Council President.

positions.stance: Pushing legislation to stop price gouging by big grocery chains and bring more grocery stores to neighborhoods that need them.
"A home should not be a luxury"; says she has fought for affordable housing since her time on the City Council.
Will protect rights "from reproductive freedom to the right to vote."
"She believes every Rhode Islander deserves to feel safe at home."

sd-gov-2026-rhoden-larry.name: Larry Rhoden
sd-gov-2026-rhoden-larry.bio: Governor of South Dakota; rancher and former lieutenant governor and state legislator.

sd-gov-2026-ahlers-dan.name: Dan Ahlers
sd-gov-2026-ahlers-dan.bio: Dell Rapids small business owner, former state legislator for District 25, and former executive director of the South Dakota Democratic Party.

positions.stance: Will invest in Main Street businesses, modernize roads, bridges and broadband, and support family farms and rural health care.
Will recruit and retain teachers, strengthen rural schools, and expand access to early childhood education and childcare.
Will support local solutions and reduce barriers to increase affordable housing for working families, seniors, and young people.
Will "fight to keep rural hospitals open," address health workforce shortages, and expand access to mental health services.
Will "fight for wages that let hardworking South Dakotans get ahead, not just get by" and invest in small businesses.

tx-gov-2026-dixon-pat.name: Pat Dixon
tx-gov-2026-dixon-pat.bio: Business owner and president of DPAS Inc., an industrial consulting firm; former Lago Vista city council member.

positions.stance: Says the governor can ask the Board of Pardons and Paroles to reconsider Robert Roberson's case: "Greg Abbott won't. I will."
Supports "free market sustainability," meaning "growth pays for itself" and those who increase demand for resources pay for them.
"As governor of Texas, I would support the ability for cities to use better voting systems"; favors Approval Voting.
Would ideally create a statewide scholarship giving every child the same amount of money to follow them to any school.
"Political parties should not override the will of the voters. We need non-partisan redistricting."

tx-ltgov-2026-cristo-anthony.name: Anthony Cristo
tx-ltgov-2026-cristo-anthony.bio: High school English and debate teacher and military veteran.

positions.stance: Says real tax relief requires cutting spending: "If we want real tax relief, we have to shrink government."
Opposes taxpayer-funded welfare but strongly supports immigrants "who come here ready to work, contribute, and succeed."
"It's time to legalize marijuana in Texas"; says the war on drugs has failed.

tx-ltgov-2026-mccormick-kevin.name: Kevin McCormick
tx-ltgov-2026-mccormick-kevin.bio: Former high school math teacher in San Antonio with a law degree from the University of Houston.

positions.stance: Says Texas cities "need transportation alternatives, especially improved public transportation and new bicycle tracks."
Proposes investing in rural Texas "to increase prosperity, sustainability, resilience, and self-reliance."
Supports ranked-choice voting, limiting gerrymandering, and other reforms to increase voters' power.
Says speculative value has replaced economic value as the basis for property tax, resulting in unfairness, and proposes reform.
"I also support Medicare for All, but affordable health care is only part of the story."
Would cut rules and fees that raise prices and treat cost of living as "the test for every state decision."
Would cut waste driving premiums up, increase insurer competition, and keep Citizens "as a backstop, not a growing substitute for a working market."
Will "fight to eliminate homestead property taxes" and force governments to cut waste instead of raising assessments.
Would strip red tape that delays home approvals and support local decisions that add starter homes and rentals.
Supports secure borders and enforcement against criminals, plus "a simpler, faster legal path" for people who come to work.

fl-gov-2026-abrams-dean.name: Dean Ocean Abrams
fl-gov-2026-abrams-dean.bio: Technology and consulting professional of about three decades, including at Microsoft, HP and KPMG.

positions.stance: Opposes Amendment 1 on budget stabilization transfers; supports Amendment 2 on agricultural equipment and Amendment 3 on the homestead exemption.
Would require insurers to publish loss ratios, use whole-company accounting, cap insurer profit, and restore policyholders' right to sue over denied claims.
Would bar institutional investors from buying single-family homes in Florida and add renter protections such as just-cause eviction.
Would pursue a waiver for the coverage gap, press to start prescription drug importation, and supports extending enhanced ACA credits as a bridge.
Would tie future minimum wage increases to Florida's cost of living and let local governments set their own wage floors.

fl-gov-2026-burkett-charles.name: Charles Burkett
fl-gov-2026-burkett-charles.bio: Former Mayor of Surfside, Florida, and former chairman of the Miami Beach Housing Authority.

positions.stance: Would "slash and eventually eliminate property taxes for vested Florida homeowners and renters" through a growing homestead exemption after ten years' residency.
"Rewrite the broken laws and bring radical competition into the property and auto insurance market."
"Reverse damage that monied interests and influential lobbyists have inflicted on local communities."
"Hold government accountable, delivering high quality services while controlling costs to residents."
"Tell the truth as to why condo owners are under financial attack after the Surfside collapse."

fl-gov-2026-dimanche-moliere.name: Moliere "Moe" Dimanche
fl-gov-2026-dimanche-moliere.bio: Host of The Moe Dimanche Show podcast.

positions.stance: Seeks to incorporate unincorporated county land across Florida into municipalities to improve public safety, 911 service, and infrastructure.
"On Day 1, Moe will permanently close Alligator Alcatraz."
Would abolish HOAs and property taxes on homesteads: "HOAs will be abolished under the Dimanche Administration."
